content.text: : recombinant human GH; growth-promoting effects mediated primarily thru ↑IGF1 – IGF-1 primary action = stim of linear growth
until epiphyseal fusion occurs near the end of puberty
Short stature assoc w/ Turner syndrome
Short stature assoc w/ Noonan syndrome
Tx of pts w/ short bowel syndrome dep on TPN
: periph edema, myalgias, arthralgias, carpal tunnel syndrome
: pseudotumor cerebri, progression of scoliosis, edema, hyperglycemia, IC HTN (vision chgs, HA, N/V), pancreatitis, gynecomastia, nevus growth
•Prader-Willi syndrome: ↑risk of asphyxiation in severely obese pts, upper airway obstruct or sleep apnea
: approved for tx of severe IGF deficiency that = ⍉responsive to hGH
: epiphyseal fusion has already occurred, existing CA, other Eti of growth failure
: hypoglycemia, IC HTN, aSx elevation of liver enzymes, enlrg tonsils, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, worsened scoliosis
: inhibits release of GH, TSH, glucagon, insulin, and gastrin
Sx control in pts w/ metastatic carcinoid tumors
Diarrhea assoc w/ vasoactive intestinal peptide-secreting tumors (VIPomas)
: GI (N/V, cramps, flatulence, steatorrhea), biliary sludge, gallstones (after 6mo of use), sinus brady, conduction disturb
: long-term tx of acromegaly that cannot be treated w/ or = unresponsive to radiation or surg
: diarrhea, GB problems, abd pain, nausea, inj site rxns

: polyethylene glycol (PEG) derivative of a mutant rhGH w altered GH-r binding sites (one site has ↑receptor affinity, and the other site has ↓affinity); allows for GH-r dimerization (initial binding step), but blocks conformational chgs needed for signal transduction; therefore, a GH-r antagonist
: tx of acromegaly in pts who have ⍉responded adequately to surg, radiation therapy, or other medical therapies or would ⍉be appropriate candidates for these therapies
: has ↑affinity for both V1A and V2 receptors; inhibits V2 receptors and → aquaresis (excretion of free H2O)
: tx of euvolemic hyponatremia in hsp pts
: hypovolemic hyponatremia, concurrent use w/ potent CYP3A inhibitors, anuric pts
: tx of pts w/ “clinically significant” hypervolemic or euvolemic hyponatremia; used in HF, cirrhosis, & SIADH

: need urgent intervention to increase serum sodium, unable to sense or respond appropriately to thirst, hypovolemic hyponatremia, concurrent use of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, ⍉forming/excreting urine
: therapy should begin or resume only in a hsp where sodium concentration can be closely monitored
